To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of the RING finger protein 5, an ER-anchoring ubiquitin ligase, is elevated and cytoplasmically mislocalized in sporadic Inclusion Body Myopathy (sIBM), a degenerative muscle disease.
the expression of a muscle ubiquitin ligase, RNF5/RMA, is elevated and deregulated in sporadic Inclusion Body Myosisis (sIBM) patients.

RNF5 is a novel factor involved in the pathogenesis and progression of s-IBM; RNF5 transgenics are a novel model for s- IBM; and RNF5 is an essential component of muscle homeostasis and its deregulation may contribute to ER stress related muscular disorders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new molecular targets in the pathogenesis and progression of s-IBM.
the role of RMA1 in the pathogenesis and pathophysiology of muscle wasting and degenerative myopathies.

the identification and characterization of ubiquitin ligase and proteasome components that are involved in muscular disorders, and the understanding of their role in the pathogenesis and progression of these conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ER-bound RING finger protein RNF5 causes degenerative myopathy and is deregulated in Inclusion body Myositis.
RNF5 plays a role in muscle regeneration, but that it is also a factor involved in the pathogenesis and progression of muscle diseases.
the ER-bound RING finger protein 5 (RMA1/RNF5) is a potential therapeutic target for sIBM and other muscle disorders associated with ER stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RNF5, an E3 ligase, plays a role in ER homeostasis and is involved in myodegeneration and muscle wasting.
RNF5 is involved in muscle regeneration, and its misexpression in the muscle leads to myodegenerative disease.
RNF5 is a key player in muscle homeostasis and its deregulation may contribute to the pathogenesis of myodegenerating diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RNF5 is a novel factor implicated in muscle degeneration, which may represent a new target for the treatment of s-IBM.
RNF5, a RING finger E2 ubiquitin ligase, is involved in the regulation of ER stress and muscle regeneration.
RNF5 is a novel factor involved in the pathophysiology of s-IBM.
